search_row.title: Neutral equilibrium heterozygosity (Kimura-Crow)
search_row.statement: Under neutral mutation to new alleles and drift, expected heterozygosity reaches an equilibrium that rises with the product of effective population size and mutation rate.

fields.dct:source: Motoo Kimura (1964) The number of alleles that can be maintained in a finite population
fields.delphi:proposedTest: Regress genome-wide neutral diversity on independent estimates of N_e times mu across species, and test whether the residual pattern is explained by linked selection.
fields.delphi:context: Assumptions: infinite-alleles mutation, neutrality, constant N_e, equilibrium. Formal status: proved within the model. Observed diversity varies far less across species than census sizes predict (Lewontin's paradox; Leffler et al. 2012), which points to linked selection and demography.
